notes: Source: official Bose Professional Technical Data Sheet (tds_pm8500n_ltr.pdf, 2015, mirrored copy verified at gaplasapro.com). All 8 analog inputs use 3-pin Phoenix Contact green terminal-block connectors (rear panel silkscreen groups them in pairs, e.g. "Input A"/"Input B" ... through H) — mapped to the closest allowed id "euroblock" (pluggable screw terminal block), consistent for the 8-pin speaker-output blocks and the 3-pin fault-relay connector (orange Phoenix Contact) as well. Speaker outputs are 2 physical 8-pin Phoenix Contact terminal-block headers on the rear panel that carry the amplifier's 2-8 configurable output channels (accepts 10-24 AWG wire) — modeled here as one representative 8-pin output connector block per Bose's own port diagram, since the datasheet does not assign individual channel-pair names to each block. AC inlet is IEC 60320-C20 (high-current IEC, mates with C19 cord) — mapped to "iec-c19". Ethernet RJ-45 (100 Mb) and rear Ethernet connector are present ONLY on the "N" (networked) variant, confirmed for PM8500N. No version/speed is stated for Ethernet beyond "100 Mb", so grade eth-100m is used. Front-panel USB Type-B port is used only for PC connection with ControlSpace Designer software; USB spec/version not stated in datasheet, so no grade was set (avoiding an unconfirmed guess). The rear panel also has a covered "Digital expansion slot" that accepts optional plug-in cards (Dante, CobraNet, AES3, ESPLink) — this is a modular bay rather than a fixed physical connector with a listed id, so it was omitted rather than force-mapped to a connector type not present without the card installed. Fault-notification output (3-pin Phoenix, NC/NO relay contact, 1A/30VDC) included as a control-style euroblock port.
